text:
maria: Heads-up — we saw a spike in downstream ingestion errors starting at ~12:05 UTC, correlated with AWS KMS p99 decrypt latency in us-west-2. Many requests hit our decrypt path and retried, causing backpressure in the consumer.
aj: Confirming, CloudWatch shows KMS ThrottlingExceptions around that time + increased latency from 14ms baseline to 800ms p99.
samir: Any service-wide outages reported by AWS? I don't see a full service degradation in the status page, looks regional flakiness.
kevin: The pipeline uses synchronous decrypt per record — that'll amplify latency. We rely on GenerateDataKey/Decrypt for each item.
jen: Which key policy/role is used? Could RBAC or an IAM change have triggered a permission fallback that caused retries?
maria: No IAM changes in the last 48h per audit log. This looks capacity-related on KMS side (throttling + semaphore stalls in our client).
aj: Short-term mitigation — can we enable a local envelope key cache for DEKs with a small TTL so we don't call KMS per message during spikes?
samir: Agreed. We already store the encrypted DEK with each blob. Proposal: cache decrypted DEKs in-memory per worker for 60s with LRU eviction and TTL. If KMS fails, use cached DEK and mark metrics.
kevin: Also add a fast-circuit-breaker: if KMS error rate > 5% in 1m, flip to "cache-first" mode and queue decryption ops to background revalidate with backoff. That prevents retries piling up.
jen: Audit concern — when we use cached DEKs we might not record a KMS Decrypt call for each item. We need to capture a signed audit event locally (and later reconcile) so compliance logs don't miss decrypts.
maria: Good point. Add a local audit entry tagged "decryption:cached" with authenticated user and request_id; batch-signed to KMS when available.
aj: Low-level: increase KMS client retry attempts and add jittered exponential backoff. Example for boto3:
``` 
from botocore.config import Config
kms_cfg = Config(retries={'max_attempts': 10, 'mode': 'standard'}, connect_timeout=1, read_timeout=5)
kms = boto3.client('kms', config=kms_cfg, region_name='us-west-2')
```
But don't rely on retries alone — that just shifts latency into the request path.
samir: For rotation: if we cache DEKs, rotation becomes trickier. DEK cache entries must be invalidated on primary key rotation. We should subscribe to key-rotation events (CloudTrail/KMS EventBridge) and invalidate cache.
kevin: Also consider multi-region CMKs and regional fallback: keep a replica key in us-east-1 and fallback decrypt requests to the other region if cross-region decrypt allowed (watch for added latency). Optionally prefetch DEKs during low traffic windows.
jen: Follow-up tasks:
- implement in-memory DEK cache + metrics (maria)
- circuit-breaker + cache-first toggle (kevin)
- local audit log entries + reconciliation process (aj)
- subscribe to rotation events + cache invalidation (samir)
- update runbooks and onboard oncall (maria)
maria: I'll open PRs for cache + metrics. Also creating a postmortem-lite for the near-miss and to document the compliance tradeoffs.
kms-bot: Incident note created: incident-20260312-kms-latency-near-miss, assigned to eng-security. Use /incident for updates.
aj: One more — let's add a targeted test in staging that injects KMS throttling (fault injection) to validate fallback and audit reconciliation.
samir: I'll own the fault-injection job. Will add an e2e that verifies no data loss and audit parity within 10m.
maria: Thanks all. We'll aim to have mitigations live behind a feature flag within 48h and default off until QA passes. :thumbsup:
